# Basics
## **Basics**

**R is free**

* Download R from <https://cran.r-project.org>

**R is a function language**

* All commands in R are regarded as functions.  
+ \texttt{plot(x, y)} produces a scatter plot of \texttt{x} vs. \texttt{y}. 

+ Help is also a function. To obtain help on the function plot use help(plot). To obtain general help use help(), i.e.use the function help with a null argument. 

+ To end a session in R use the function quit().

**R is an object orientated language**

* All entities in R are objects. This includes vectors, matrices, data arrays, graphs, functions, and results of an analysis. 

-------------

**Basics**

To create a vector of numbers, we use the function \texttt{c()}

```{r}
x <- c(1,3,2,5) 
x
```

The length of a vector is found using the \texttt{length()} function.

```{r}
length(x)
```


--------------

 **Basics**

To create a matrix of numbers, we use the function \texttt{matrix()}

```{r}
y <- matrix(c(1,2,3,4), 2, 2)
y
```

Take the square-root of each element of the matrix \texttt{y}
```{r}
sqrt(y)
```

-----------

## **Basics**

Square each element of the matrix \texttt{y}
```{r}
y^2
```

The square of the matrix \texttt{y}
```{r}
y%*%y
```

-------------------

**Basics**

Sequence vectors can be created in several ways.

```{r}
seq(1,10, 1)
seq(1,10, length=10)
seq(1,10)
1:10
```

---------------

**Basics**

More sequences

```{r}
seq(1,10, 2)
seq(1,10, length=5)
rep(1,4)
rep(1:4, 3)
```


---------

**Basics**

Matrices

```{r}
diag(3)
matrix(1,3,4)
```

-----------

**Basics**

More matrices

```{r}
matrix(1:4, 3, 4, byrow=TRUE)
outer(1:3, 1:3, "+")/2
```


---------------------

 **Basics**

Binding vectors into matrices

```{r}
x <- c(1,2,3)
y <- seq(4,6)
rbind(x,y)
cbind(x,y)
```


------------------

**Basics**

Data frames

```{r}
subjects <- c('Jim','Jack','Joe','Mary','Jean')
sex <- c('M', 'M', 'M', 'F', 'F')
score <- c(85,90,75,100,70)
D2 <- data.frame(subjects,sex,score)
D2
```

----------------

**Basics**

Operations on data frames

```{r}
D2$score
mean(D2$score)
with(D2, mean(score))
```

------------------

**Basics**

Adding a new variable

```{r}
D2$letter<-c('B', 'A', 'C', 'A', 'C')
D2
```

----------------

**Reading Data** 

- Read the Botswana average monthly temperature data into $R$.

```{r, warning=F, message=F}
library(readr)
BW <- read_csv("C:/Users/zidanac/OneDrive - biust.ac.bw/BIUST/STAT 303 Linear regression/R lectures/BWtemp.csv")
head(BW, 4)
```
----------------

**Check Data**

```{r}
is.data.frame(BW)
is.matrix(BW)
```

--------------

**Working with Data** 

Drop a variable
```{r}
BW$Country <- NULL
head(BW)
```

-------------------


```{r}
str(BW)

```

-----------------

**Working with Data** 

- Calculate the average annual temperature

```{r}
BW.y <- aggregate(Temperature ~ Year, data=BW, mean)
head(BW.y, 3)
BW.y <- with(BW, tapply(Temperature, Year, mean))
head(BW.y, 3)
```

-------------------------

**Working with Data** 

Calculate the average of all variables
```{r}
colMeans(BW)
BW.m <- as.matrix(BW)
apply(BW.m, 2, mean)
```

----------------------

**Working with Dataframes** 

Referencing values in a matrix
```{r}
BW.m[1,2]
BW.m[1:3,1:2]
```

---

```{r}
BW.m[2,]
BW.m[2,c(1,3)]
BW.m[2,-1]
```

-----------------

**Installing and Loading Packages**

- to install packages u=you ned to write the following command:*install.packages("ggplot2")*

- Loading a package in the workpace: *library(ggplot2)*

- load data in the workspace: 


```{r loadpack, warning=FALSE, message=F}
library(ggplot2)
## Use and load data in work space
data("txhousing")
data("mpg")
```

---------------------


```{r}
head(mpg)
```

# Graphics

**Enter Data**


```{r data1}
## House Price
HP = c(245,312,279,308,199,219,405,324,319,255)
##size of house
X=c(1400,1600,1700,1875,1100,1550,2350,2450,1425,1700) 
df1 = as.data.frame(cbind(X, HP))
```

------------------------

**Histogram of House Price**

```{r}
with(df1, hist(HP))
```


---------------------------

 **Scatter Plot  basis**

```{r}
with(df1, plot(X, HP))
```

------------------

**Graphics with dplyr and ggplot2

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
df1%>%
  ggplot(aes(X, HP))+
  geom_point()+theme_bw()
  
```

-------------------------------

**Boxplot Graphics**

- A comparison boxplot of Month vs. Temperature.

```{r}
with(BW, boxplot(Temperature ~ Month))
```
